There is opposition besides myself, particularly from protocol developers about gas incentives they will optimize around. There are some good ideas bouncing around. the most taxing thing to ACD time was having to discuss and explicitly reject those bogus proposals those _protocol developers in opposition_ are mostly in your head, I'm afraid I read some of their posts in the call. You're free to respond to them on the forum. But please reduce your hostility to me. We have a lot in common and share similar values. I will respond where I see fit, thank you. As I said, please don't try to steer discussion of the EIP you're opposed to. Under state-expiry, we differentiate between zero and unset. This is a change from the current way we use the trie. Once something is set, I don't believe it can ever go back to unset, and thus, the trie is forced to hold the "zero" value forever. I'm not 100% certain, but I believe this dictates that we **must** remove refunds for setting things back to zero because under the state expiry scheme, setting things to zero doesn't actually free up storage....
